rationale: Roberts is likely to keep the opinion narrow and Dan’s City-centered, holding that a personal-injury negligent-selection claim lacks the requisite nexus “with respect to the transportation of property,” while treating the safety exception as corroborative rather than essential. The dissent is most likely led by Thomas (possibly with Barrett writing separately) emphasizing Morales/Rowe breadth and the view that negligent selection directly regulates a broker’s core service and falls outside the motor-vehicle safety carveout.
